subject: Banking
title: Central Bank Digital Currencies
description: A short lesson to help you apply Central Bank Digital Currencies.

hook.text: 130 countries are exploring digital versions of their currencies. China's digital yuan already has 260 million users.

buildup.text: CBDCs are government-issued digital money. Unlike crypto, they are centrally controlled and backed by the state.

discovery.text: CBDCs could make payments instant, free, and universal. Everyone with a phone would have a central bank account.

twist.text: CBDCs give governments full visibility into every transaction. Financial privacy could vanish with state digital money.

climax.text: CBDCs promise inclusion and efficiency but threaten privacy.

punchline.text: Digital government money for everyone. Total access, total visibility.

quiz.question: What is a key concern about central bank digital currencies?
options: Governments could track every transaction, eliminating financial privacy

details.summary: Central bank digital currencies are government-issued digital money that functions like cash but exists only electronically, allowing central banks to offer a digital payment option that does not depend on commercial banks.
details.whyItMatters: CBDCs could give governments direct tools for monetary policy, financial inclusion, and payment system resilience while raising unprecedented questions about privacy and state surveillance of transactions.
takeaways: Over 130 countries are exploring or piloting CBDC programs
China's digital yuan is the most advanced major economy CBDC
CBDCs could enable programmable money with automatic conditions

faq.question: How is a CBDC different from cryptocurrency?
faq.answer: A CBDC is issued and controlled by a central bank, backed by the full faith of the government. Cryptocurrencies are decentralized and uncontrolled. A CBDC has stable value by design; crypto fluctuates with markets.

faq.question: Could CBDCs let governments track all your spending?
faq.answer: Potentially, yes. Unlike cash, digital transactions leave records. Design choices about privacy will determine whether CBDCs are anonymous like cash or fully traceable. This is the most debated aspect of CBDC development.
